transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I came in because... I just feel like I got a motor running inside me all day, you know? Like it never shuts off. It's real bad if I have to sit still. Like at church, or sitting out there in the waiting room, or even just at home trying to watch TV. I just feel trapped, like I'm gonna jump out of my skin, and I have to get up and do something. Speaking of church, Pastor Dave was talking about patience this Sunday, and I thought, man, I'd love to have some of that, but my buddy Earl—he sits two pews up—he bought this old Chevy truck he's been fixing up, and I told him he needs to check the carburetor because those things are always acting up, but he wouldn't listen to me. I used to work on cars all the time before... well, anyway, yeah, I just can't sit still. It's driving me crazy.
Did this restless feeling start after you began a new medicine or changed the dose of one?

No, I ain't taking any new pills or nothing. I don't even really like taking medicine, to be honest with you. My aunt Linda, she takes a whole handful of 'em every morning. She’s got one of those plastic boxes with the days of the week on it, you know? Except the letters rubbed off hers, so she's always getting them mixed up. She had this little terrier dog that actually chewed on the Tuesday compartment once. Man, that dog was crazy... always digging holes under the fence. I had to go over there and put some chicken wire down in the dirt so it wouldn't get out into the street. Took me like three hours in the hot sun, and I didn't even have a proper pair of wire cutters, just these rusty old pliers. But uh... what were you asking? Oh, right, my medicine. Nah, I haven't started anything new.
Do you ever have times when you feel unusually up or euphoric?

Euphoric? Like... like super happy? Nah, I don't think so. I mean, I get in a good mood sometimes, sure, but not like... not like crazy happy or nothing. Like the other day, I found a twenty dollar bill in the pocket of my old winter coat. I was pretty happy about that. I was just digging in there looking for my keys because I locked myself out of the house again. I do that all the time. Last time I had to pry the screen off the bathroom window, and it bent the frame, so now the bugs get in. We had this huge moth in the living room last night, just flying around the lamp, driving me nuts. I tried to swat it with a rolled-up magazine—it was one of those hunting magazines my cousin gets in the mail. He actually shot a buck last season, ten-pointer. He sent me a picture of it on his phone, but his phone screen is all cracked, so you could barely see the antlers. He dropped it when we were out fishing on the lake. The phone, I mean. But no, I don't get super happy or nothing like that. Just regular, I guess.
Have you been this fidgety and unable to sit still since you were a kid?

Oh, yeah. Ever since I was a little kid. Back when I was a boy in school, the teachers were always moving my seat around because I just could not stay put. I was always talking out of turn, and I'd get in big trouble for jumping up before class was even done. Speaking of class being done, they had this really loud bell at my elementary school. Sounded exactly like a fire alarm. Actually, one time, Jimmy Henderson pulled the real fire alarm on a dare. We all had to stand out in the freezing snow for like an hour. Jimmy’s dad owned the hardware store downtown—well, it used to be a hardware store, but now it’s one of those fancy coffee shops where they charge you like six bucks for a tiny little cup. I went in there once and asked for just a regular black coffee, and the guy behind the counter looked at me like I had two heads. He had this weird mustache, you know, the kind you gotta wax so it curls up at the ends? Looked like a cartoon villain or something. I don't know how he drinks anything without getting it all up in his hair. Honestly, I'd just shave it off. It just seems like a lot of work every morning. But... wait, what were you asking me? Something about school?
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Worrying? I mean, not really. I don't sit around chewing my nails over stuff, if that's what you mean. I got a buddy, Carl, he worries about everything. He's got this old Ford pickup, right? And he's always convinced the transmission is about to drop right out of the bottom of it. I told him, "Carl, you just gotta check the fluid," but he won't listen. He keeps talking about taking it to this mechanic out on Route 9, but that guy is a total rip-off. He charged my brother-in-law four hundred dollars just to look at his brakes. And my brother-in-law, he's not exactly rolling in dough right now because he got laid off from the bottling plant. They shut the whole place down last month. Said something about supply chain issues, but I think the owner just wanted to sell the land to some developers. They're putting up those ugly townhouses everywhere now, the ones with the fake brick on the front and nothing but vinyl siding on the back. They built a whole row of 'em right behind the old bowling alley. Used to love that bowling alley. They had this arcade machine in the corner, Pac-Man, but the joystick always stuck to the left. You had to slam it really hard to get him to turn right. Cost me so many quarters... I used to keep a whole jar of quarters in my room just for that. But nah, I don't really worry about stuff too much. I just kind of go with the flow, you know?
